}}'''Günther Wilke''' (23 February 1925 – 9 December 2016) was a German chemist who was influential in [[organometallic chemistry]].  He was the director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]] (Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung) from 1967–1992, succeeding [[Karl Ziegler]] in that post.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kofo.mpg.de/de/institut/geschichte |title=History of the Max-Planck-Institute (German) |access-date=2013-06-22 |archive-date=2019-04-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426094046/http://www.kofo.mpg.de/de/institut/geschichte |url-status=dead }}</ref>  During Wilke's era, the MPI made several discoveries and achieved some financial independence from patents and a gift from the Ziegler family.  The institute continued as a center of excellence in organometallic chemistry.

Wilke's own area of interest focused on [[homogeneous catalysis]] by [[nickel]] complexes. His group discovered or developed several compounds including [[Bis(cyclooctadiene)nickel(0)|Ni(1,5-cyclooctadiene)<sub>2</sub>]], Ni([[allyl]])<sub>2</sub>, Ni([[ethylene|C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>]])<sub>3</sub>.  Some of these complexes are useful [[catalyst]]s for the [[oligomerization]] of [[diene]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | author=Wilke, G.| title=Contributions to Organo-Nickel Chemistry | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English | volume= 27 | pages=185–206 | year=1988 | doi=10.1002/anie.198801851}}</ref> He died in 2016 at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/10207261/Gunther_Wilke_1925__2016.html |title=Günther Wilke (1925 – 2016) |publisher=ChemistryViews.org |date=13 December 2016 |access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>

[[File:Ni(cod)2.png|thumb|left|220px|Wilke is credited with the discovery of [[bis(cyclooctadiene)nickel(0)]], a useful [[homogeneous catalyst]].]]

==Honours and awards==
* Seven honorary doctorates
* corresponding member of the math and science class abroad
* [[Wilhelm Exner Medal]] in 1980.<ref name=Editor/>
* Former Vice President of the [[Max Planck Society]] (1978-1990)
* Member of the North Rhine-Westphalian Academy of Science (President 1994-1997)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.awk.nrw.de/akademie/klassen/naturmedizin/ordentliche-mitglieder/wilke-guenther.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324092133/http://www.awk.nrw.de/akademie/klassen/naturmedizin/ordentliche-mitglieder/wilke-guenther.html |title=Professor Dr. rer. nat., Dr. Eh., Dr. h.c. mult. Günther Wilke |publisher=Nordrhein-Westfälischen Akademie der Wissenschaften |archive-date=24 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], Halle
* Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]
* Foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1977)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/5009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214205557/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/5009 |title=G.W. Wilke |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=14 February 2016 |access-date=14 February 2016}}</ref>
* [[Austrian Decoration for Science and Art]]
* President of the [[German Chemical Society]] (''Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker'')
* Chairman of the Society of German Scientists and Physicians
* [[Grand Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] (1987)
